signals.text:
fix(seq): respect known length lower bounds when minting fresh model values

theory_seq::mk_value's fallback for unresolved internal sequence values
(added for #9063) called value_factory::get_fresh_value(sort), which for
strings always mints a short fixed-pattern placeholder ("!0!", "!1!", ...)
with no awareness of constraints already derived elsewhere in the solver.

When a term's length lower bound is established via solved equalities and
arithmetic propagation (e.g. str.len(f(x)) >= 5 propagated onto a term
solved-equal to f(x)), the resulting fresh value could be shorter than that
bound, producing an internally inconsistent model (caught by
model_validate=true but otherwise silently returned to the user).

Fix: reuse the existing theory_seq::lower_bound2 helper to query any known
length lower bound on the original term, and pad the fresh string value to
meet it before it is used as a model value.

Fixes #7664 (first/original reproducer; a second reproducer attached to the
issue no longer reproduces independently of this change).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
